title: attachment-text — case shape (v0.1)
description: Pins one byte-level case for protocol::encode_attachment_text_blob_raw + protocol::decode_attachment_text_blob — the MYE1 per-attachment extracted-text codec (MYND-328; §9.15). Each attachment whose text has been extracted gets a per-attachment cache blob at attachments-text/<attachment-id-hex>, sealed under attachment_text_key = DeriveSubkey(root_key, SubkeyRole::AttachmentTextKey). The inner plaintext is OPAQUE bytes (the desktop layer's postcard ExtractedText struct) — the structural twin of vault-search / vault-dictionary. The AAD (aad_attachment_text_blob, role 'attachment-text-blob') binds account_number_hash AND the attachment_id (so one KEK is safe across all attachment-text blobs) AND the extractor_version byte. The HKDF role 'attachment-text-key' is DISTINCT from the AAD role 'attachment-text-blob'. Four case kinds: 'encrypt' (encoder byte output), 'decrypt_ok' (round-trip success), 'decrypt_aead_fail' (non-distinguishing AEAD failure per spec §6.4 — incl. wrong attachment_id), 'parse_fail' (distinguishable pre-decryption structural reject, one per AttachmentTextBlobError decode variant). The Rust reference implementation lives at protocol/src/attachment_text_blob.rs (main myne repository); spec contract is docs/spec/protocol.md §9.15 + §3.4 + §5.2.

vector_id.description: Stable identifier of the form 'attachment-text/v0.1/<descriptive-slug>'. Immutable once shipped — downstream test runners may reference these strings.

oneOf.title: encrypt — pin the encoder's byte output

input_root_key_hex.description: 32-byte root_key (hex). The runner derives attachment_text_key from this via the canonical derive_subkey helper (SubkeyRole::AttachmentTextKey, role string 'attachment-text-key') before calling the encoder.

input_account_number_hash_hex.description: 16-byte account_number_hash (hex). Bound into the 82-byte AAD via aad_attachment_text_blob (role string 'attachment-text-blob' — DISTINCT from the HKDF role 'attachment-text-key').

input_attachment_id_hex.description: 32-byte attachment_id (hex), the content-addressed id of the source MYA1 attachment. Bound into the AAD so a blob sealed for attachment A cannot AEAD-verify served as attachment B — the per-blob binding that makes one KEK safe across all attachment-text blobs.

input_plaintext_hex.description: Opaque inner-plaintext bytes (hex), variable length including zero. The codec treats these as client-opaque (the desktop layer's postcard ExtractedText struct); there is no canonical-JSON discipline here.

input_nonce_hex.description: 24-byte XChaCha20-Poly1305 nonce (hex). Production callers source from OS CSPRNG; vectors pin a constant.

informational_attachment_text_key_hex.description: 32-byte HKDF output (hex), pre-computed from root_key via derive_subkey(SubkeyRole::AttachmentTextKey). Informational — verified implicitly via the expected_attachment_text_blob_hex assertion; carried so reviewers don't have to re-derive to inspect intermediate state.

expected_attachment_text_blob_hex.description: Full encoder output (34-byte header + ciphertext + 32-byte CTX tag), hex-encoded lowercase. Decoders compare byte-equal. The v0.1 extractor_version byte (0x01) sits at header offset 5.

oneOf.title: decrypt_ok — pin the decoder's successful round-trip

expected_plaintext_hex.description: Recovered opaque inner-plaintext bytes (hex), empty allowed. The decoder returns these for the desktop layer to deserialize.

oneOf.title: decrypt_aead_fail — pin the non-distinguishing failure surface

expected_kind.description: The decoder MUST report a non-distinguishing AEAD failure (Rust reference: AttachmentTextBlobError::CannotDecrypt). Implementations MUST NOT distinguish cross-vault (wrong account_number_hash) vs wrong attachment_id vs tampered ciphertext/tag vs wrong key beyond the single 'cannot decrypt' outcome (spec §6.4). Structurally distinguishable rejects (bad magic, unsupported extractor_version, etc.) are pinned separately under case_kind 'parse_fail'.

oneOf.title: parse_fail — pin a distinguishable pre-decryption structural reject

input_blob_hex.description: A structurally malformed blob (hex), empty allowed. The decoder rejects it BEFORE attempting any decryption — magic / protocol_version / extractor_version / length checks all run before the AEAD stage (spec §9.15.1 magic-byte-before-decrypt discipline).

expected_error.description: The specific structural reject the decoder MUST surface (Rust reference: AttachmentTextBlobError::{MagicMismatch, ProtocolVersionMismatch, ExtractorVersionUnsupported, HeaderTooShort, CiphertextTruncated, CiphertextLenOverflow}). Unlike the AEAD failure surface (case_kind decrypt_aead_fail), these are pre-decryption and intentionally distinguishable: a port must reject e.g. a future extractor_version cleanly so the caller re-extracts from the MYA1 source (§9.15.4).
